Some vaccines contain weakened or inactive parts of a virus or bacterium, while mRNA vaccines use instructions that help cells produce a harmless protein fragment. Childhood vaccination programs have helped reduce diseases such as measles and polio in many countries. Because vaccines prevent every infection completely, vaccinated people do not need other public health measures during outbreaks.
claim_text: mRNA vaccines use instructions that help cells produce a harmless protein fragment.
evidence_summary: FDA says some vaccines contain genetic material for a specific protein and direct the body to produce a small amount of that protein, which the immune system detects. The claim is supported at a general level.
evaluator_note_en: The evidence supports the general mechanism of mRNA vaccines. No correction is needed.
